arguments.text: Request #1 fixed. Bug: Interval.fromISO called DateTime.fromISO on each half without guarding against Settings.throwOnInvalid, so a valid "<start>/<duration>" (or "<duration>/<end>") string threw an InvalidDateTimeError instead of being parsed as a Duration. Fixed by wrapping each DateTime.fromISO in try/catch and treating a throw as "not a valid DateTime", so the duration branch is reached and unparsable input still yields Interval.invalid (which throws InvalidIntervalError when throwOnInvalid is set). Verified: the three valid ISO forms no longer throw with throwOnInvalid=true, invalid input still throws, and non-throwing mode still returns an invalid Interval. Full test suite: no new failures (only the 2 pre-existing toFormat locale failures remain).

Request #2 fixed. Bug: in src/impl/util.js, objToLocalTS converted a calendar object with Date.UTC (which maps years 0-99 to 19XX) and then only corrected the year via setUTCFullYear(getUTCFullYear() - 1900). Because the intermediate 19XX/20XX year has a different leap-year structure than the target year (2000 is a leap year, 100 is not), day-of-month overflow was computed against the wrong February, so e.g. DateTime.fromISO("0099-12-31").plus({ days: 61 }) returned 0100-03-01 instead of 0100-03-02. Fixed by re-setting year, month and day together: d.setUTCFullYear(obj.year, obj.month - 1, obj.day), so the overflow is resolved against the correct year. Verified with a brute-force comparison of plus/minus across years 90-110 against a proleptic-Gregorian reference (0 mismatches, previously 13), plus the existing "100 barrier" tests. Full suite: no new failures.

arguments.text: Working on it. Diagnosis so far: in src/datetime.js, isInDST compares the current offset against the offsets at `set({ month: 1 })` and `set({ month: 5 })`. In 1974 the US was on DST from Jan 6 to Oct 27, so for a date in that window `set({ month: 1 })` lands inside DST too (and for January dates it is a no-op), both comparisons come out equal and isInDST wrongly returns false. Fix: compare against fixed reference dates (Jan 1 / May 1) so the standard-time offset is always found. Will verify against the 1974 America/New_York transition dates and re-run the full suite.
Received; will diagnose Duration#normalize's unit-pair conversion table in src/duration.js next, after finishing the isInDST fix I'm in the middle of. ETA ~12 minutes.
#2 (objToLocalTS 100-year barrier through February): fixed and verified.
#4 (isInDST in 1974): still in progress — fix identified (compare against fixed reference dates Jan 1 / May 1 instead of set({month:1})/set({month:5})), verifying now. ETA ~3 min.
#5 (Duration#normalize unit pairs): still in progress, not started in earnest yet (finishing #4 first). ETA ~10 min.

arguments.text: #2 fixed and verified (objToLocalTS year-100 barrier through February).
#4 fixed and verified (isInDST now compares against fixed Jan 1 / May 1 reference dates, so 1974 America/New_York reports DST from Jan 6 02:00 through Oct 27 02:00).

#5 fixed and verified (Duration conversion matrices were incomplete: added the missing `quarters: 4` to years and `seconds` to quarters in the casual matrix, plus `quarters: 4` in the longterm matrix). All unit pairs now convert in both conversion accuracies; all 121 duration tests pass.
#7 fixed and verified (padStart in src/impl/util.js now handles negative numbers, so DateTime#toISODate() gives "-0001-01-01" instead of "00-1-01-01").
#8 fixed and verified (FixedOffsetZone#isValid now returns isNumber(this.fixed) instead of always true, so a non-numeric offset makes the zone — and any DateTime built in it — invalid).
